title: Garmin watch face (wfb format 1)
description: The normative definition of the wfb authoring format. Point a YAML language server at this file to get autocomplete and inline validation while authoring.

format.description: Format major version. The compiler refuses a version it does not understand rather than parsing it partially (ADR 0009).

targets.description: Device ids to build for by default. Must be installed Connect IQ device definitions. The CLI's -d/--device replaces this set, and may name devices not listed here.

antialias.description: Face-wide default for anti-aliasing. Defaults to false, matching the platform's own default -- a crisp 1-bit bitmap font, and non-anti-aliased Dc primitives (a guarded 'dc has :setAntiAlias' call around a shape, progress, graph, hands or pattern element's own drawing). Every font, icon and primitive-drawing element inherits this unless it declares its own 'antialias:' (a group's own value becomes the default for its subtree in turn, so only the nearest enclosing declaration matters). Anti-aliasing a font costs runtime RAM the resource compiler does not report anywhere the build can measure (SDK: Resources, Fonts); anti-aliasing a shape, progress, graph, hands or pattern element on a 64-colour panel (every currently supported target) dithers its soft edge, reported by the suppressible 'antialias-dither' lint -- turn it on only where the softer edge is worth either cost.

min_1px.description: Face-wide default for whether a nonzero relative ('%'/'%r') size, thickness, 'bar_width:' or an element/part's own radius clamps up to at least 1 px instead of rounding away to nothing (sign preserved) -- the same hairline that draws as 1 px on one screen can otherwise round to 0 on another. Defaults to false: a face that never writes 'min_1px:' compiles to byte-identical output. Every 'group', 'shape', 'progress', 'graph', 'hands', 'pattern' element and hand/pattern part inherits this unless it declares its own 'min_1px:' (a group's own value becomes the default for its whole subtree in turn, and a hand/pattern part's own value wins outright over its element's) -- nearest declaration wins at every level, overriding either way, exactly the shape 'antialias:' uses. Only a size (width/height), thickness, 'bar_width:' or an element/part's own radius is affected -- never a position ('at:', 'to:', a polygon's points, a linear pattern's 'step:'), 'corner_radius:', a 'px'/'pt' length or an author-written exact 0. Not accepted on 'text', 'icon' or 'complication_slot': a font size (including an icon's 'size:'/'icon_size:') already floors at 1 px on its own path (no switch needed). Whenever this is off and a relative length would have been clamped, the suppressible 'sub-pixel-length' lint reports it.

aod.description: Face-wide always-on-display (AOD) defaults, for an AMOLED target (docs/plans/14-aod.md). Sits beside 'elements:', not inside it.

palette.description: Named colours. Elements reference palette entries, never raw hex. Each entry is either the short form (a colour directly) or the long form ({value, label}), which adds a human-readable label a 'config:' choices: entry can pick up by referencing this entry as 'palette.<name>'.

fonts.description: Custom bitmap fonts, baked from a TrueType source at build time. Only the glyphs the design actually uses are rendered into the sheet.

color_scheme.description: Named role -> colour sets, picked on-device via a 'config: style:' entry's 'colors:' -- the Styles axis, the only one Garmin's native editor gives no meaning to (docs/research/09-data-library-and-config-axes.md §3). Every entry must declare the identical set of roles, or 'config.colors.<role>' would be undefined whenever the wearer picks a style entry that lacks it.

config.description: User-editable colours, read through the fēnix 8's native on-device watch face editor (API 5.1.0). Garmin offers exactly two colour axes -- one accent colour, one data colour -- plus the Styles axis, which carries no colour of its own but is the only one Garmin gives no meaning to, so this compiler gives each listed 'style:' entry a meaning: a declared 'color_scheme:' (and, from a later phase, a layout). The axis is the key rather than an author-chosen name; declaring a fourth would need a feature Garmin does not have. Reference a declared colour entry as an ordinary colour expression, e.g. 'color: config.accent_color' or 'color: config.colors.<role>'. A target with no native editor (fr955) keeps every declared default -- see the suppressible 'config-unsupported' warning.

accent_color.description: The one native accent-colour axis (<accentColors> in the generated resource, Settings.accentColor read back).

data_color.description: The one native data-colour axis (<dataColors> in the generated resource, Settings.complicationColor read back).

style.description: The Styles axis: an ordered list of author-named entries (<styles> in the generated resource, Settings.styleId read back -- index = entry position). Each entry names a declared 'color_scheme:' entry as 'colors:', a declared 'layouts:' entry as 'layout:', or both. Replaces the earlier 'config: colors:' outright (removed, no shim).

data.description: The Data axis: named native complication slots (<data> in the generated resource, Settings.complicationSettings read back). Each entry's 'default:'/'choices:' name 'complication.<name>' types (see 'wfb complications'), not colours or schemes. Drawn by a 'type: complication_slot' element referencing it as 'slot: config.data.<name>'.

elements.description: The layer tree. Z-order is document order unless z is given.

static.description: Elements that never change, gathered in one place. Exactly equivalent to writing a single 'group' with 'static: true' as the first entry of 'elements:' -- which is what the compiler rewrites it to, under the reserved id 'static'. Accepts the same two spellings as 'elements:': a list of elements, or a mapping whose key is the element id.

layouts.description: Named widget sets the wearer switches between on-device, form A only (docs/guide/styles-and-layouts.md) -- there is no element-level membership key. Each entry's 'static:'/'elements:' are folded at build time into two synthetic groups appended to the top-level 'elements:' (see 'wfb/desugar.py'); this compiler's own schema check runs after that fold, so by then each body here is just '{}' or '{lint: ...}'. A declared entry that no 'config: style:' choice names as its 'layout:' is an error -- nothing would let the wearer pick it -- and a 'complication_slot' may not appear inside one (the Data axis is face-wide; it belongs in the shared top-level 'elements:').

hands.description: Named analog-hand sets (plan 04): hour/minute/second, each a list of primitives drawn pointing at 12 o'clock in a frame whose origin is the axis. Declared once, placed on screen by a 'type: hands' element naming one by name -- so several sets may coexist and switch with Styles ('layouts:').

align.description: Which horizontal edge of this element's placement box sits at the point 'at:' resolves to (left/right), or its centre (docs/guide/placement.md, "Placement: at: and align:").

verticalAlign.description: Which vertical edge of this element's placement box sits at the point 'at:' resolves to (top/bottom), or its centre (docs/guide/placement.md, "Placement: at: and align:"). 'baseline' was renamed 'bottom' -- it always meant the box's bottom edge, never a typographic baseline.

elementListOrMapping.description: A list of elements, or a mapping whose key is the element id -- the shape 'static:', a layout's own 'static:'/'elements:', and (via the desugar rewrite) 'elements:' itself all share.

layout.description: One 'layouts:' entry: this layout's own fixed and per-frame content, drawn on top of the design's shared 'static:'/'elements:' while this layout is the active one (docs/guide/styles-and-layouts.md). A 'complication_slot' may not appear in either -- the Data axis is face-wide, so a slot belongs in the shared top-level 'elements:'.

static.description: This layout's own fixed furniture, drawn once into the shared static buffer while this layout is active, after the design's shared static content. Same two spellings as the top-level 'static:'.

elements.description: This layout's own elements, drawn every frame while this layout is active, above the design's shared elements. Same two spellings as the top-level 'elements:'.

id.description: The Connect IQ application UUID. Generate once and keep it stable; changing it makes the watch treat the face as a different app.

entry.description: Monkey C entry class name. Derived from the face name when omitted.

color.description: A literal colour, or a reference to a palette or config entry. 'config.<axis>' is two segments (accent_color/data_color); 'config.colors.<role>' is three, one role of the Styles axis -- both accepted here so a misused reference (e.g. a palette entry naming one) reaches the friendlier IR-level error instead of failing schema validation with no context.

hexColor.description: A literal colour, '#RRGGBB' or '#RGB'. Not a palette/config reference -- used where a build-time literal is required, such as a 'config:' entry's own 'default:' and 'choices:'.

paletteEntry.description: Long form of a 'palette:' entry: an explicit colour plus a human-readable label. The label is otherwise inert -- it surfaces only when this entry is referenced from a 'config:' 'default:'/'choices:' as 'palette.<name>', where it becomes the same '<color label="@Strings...">' and generated '<string>' an inline 'label:' on a choices: item produces today.

value.description: The entry's colour -- a literal '#RRGGBB'/'#RGB', same restriction as the short form: a palette entry may not reference 'config.*' (or another 'palette.*' entry).

label.description: Shown in the editor's picker when this entry is used as a 'config:' choice. Optional -- an entry with no label used as a choice produces an unlabelled '<color>', same as omitting 'label:' on an inline choice.

paletteRef.description: A reference to a named 'palette:' entry, accepted where a build-time literal colour is otherwise required (a 'config:' entry's 'default:'/'choices:').

configColor.description: One native colour axis: a compiled-in default, plus either the editor's full colour picker ('any') or an explicit, orderable list of choices. Every declared colour is checked against the target's 64-colour palette rule, the same 'palette-dither' check a palette entry gets.

default.description: Compiled into the view as the starting value, and the only value a device without the native editor (fr955) ever shows -- not a fallback path, the path. A literal colour, or a 'palette.<name>' reference -- either way it must also appear (by colour value) in 'choices:' when 'choices:' is an explicit list.

choices.description: 'any' hands the wearer the editor's own full colour picker (allowAny="true", no listed colours, no string resources needed). An explicit list becomes the editor's picklist; 'default:' must be one of the listed colours in that case, since Garmin defines no behaviour for a default that is not in the list.

configChoice.description: One entry in an explicit 'choices:' list -- either a bare 'palette.<name>' reference (contributing that entry's colour and, if it has one, its label) or an inline {color, label}.

label.description: Shown in the editor's picker. Optional -- an unlabelled colour is legal (the SDK's own sample has one) and becomes a '<color>' with no label attribute.

colorScheme.description: One 'color_scheme:' entry: an optional editor label plus a role -> colour mapping. Every color_scheme entry in a design must declare the identical set of roles.

label.description: Shown in the editor's Styles list. Optional -- a scheme with none produces a '<style>' with no label attribute.

colors.description: Role name -> colour, either a literal '#RRGGBB'/'#RGB' or a 'palette.<name>' reference.

configStyle.description: The Styles axis: an author-named, ordered set of entries -- each one line of the editor's Style list (plan 02 §4.1, §12.4). Unlike 'accent_color'/'data_color', entries are named by the author rather than by colour value, so 'default:' names an entry, not a scheme.

default.description: The entry (a 'choices:' key) compiled into the view as the starting styleId, and the only entry a device without the native editor (fr955) ever shows -- not a fallback path, the path. Must be one of 'choices:'.

choices.description: The editor's Styles picklist, an ordered mapping of entry name -> entry -- editor order, and the order '<style id="N">' numbers entries from (index 0 first). There is no 'any' here, unlike the two colour axes: Styles has no equivalent of the editor's own unrestricted picker.

styleEntry.description: One 'config: style:' entry: at least one of 'layout:'/'colors:', plus an optional 'label:' and 'lint:' (docs/guide/styles-and-layouts.md).

label.description: Shown in the editor's Styles list. Optional -- an entry with no label and only 'colors:' (no 'layout:') falls back to that scheme's own 'label:'; every other entry with no 'label:' of its own gets no label attribute.

layout.description: Names a declared 'layouts:' entry by its bare name (e.g. 'layout: digital'). Required on every entry once 'layouts:' is declared, and rejected when it is not -- an entry showing only shared content in a design that has layouts would be a silent blank-looking face.

colors.description: Names a declared 'color_scheme:' entry by its bare name (e.g. 'colors: dark'), not the 'color_scheme.<name>' reference form used inside expressions. Every entry in one 'choices:' must carry 'colors:', or none may.

complicationRef.description: A reference to a 'wfb.complications' type, accepted from a 'config: data:' slot's own 'default:'/'choices:' -- the same table 'on_hold:' resolves against (run 'wfb complications' for the full list).

configDataSlot.description: One 'config: data:' entry: a compiled-in default complication type plus either the editor's full complication picker ('any') or an explicit, orderable list of choices. Drawn by a 'type: complication_slot' element referencing this slot by name.

default.description: Compiled into the view as the starting Complications.Id, and the only type a device without the native editor (fr955) ever shows -- not a fallback path, the path. Must also appear in 'choices:' when 'choices:' is an explicit list.

choices.description: 'any' hands the wearer the editor's own unrestricted complication picker (allowAny="true", no listed types). Superseded 2026-09-13: 'any' used to also forbid 'icon_size:' on any element referencing this slot, since the set of icons an unbounded picker could need was unbounded -- lifted once every native complication type had a catalogue icon (wfb.icons.COMPLICATION_ICON covers all 42 now), so 'icon_size:' is accepted there too: it resolves against the whole of that table, and a Connect IQ-app complication (outside it) simply draws no icon. An explicit list becomes the editor's picklist; 'default:' must be one of the listed types in that case, compared by resolved type regardless of which item shape named it.

configDataChoice.description: One 'choices:' entry in an explicit 'config: data:' list: either a bare 'complication.<name>' reference (today's only form), or a mapping naming the same reference plus a per-choice icon override -- 'icon:' (a catalogue name, or the literal 'none' to explicitly draw no icon for this choice) or 'glyph:' (any codepoint in the vendored icon font, 'U+XXXX'), mutually exclusive with each other. Absent from a plain bare reference, this per-choice icon overrides wfb.icons.COMPLICATION_ICON's catalogue default for that one type; every other choice keeps using the catalogue default (or draws none, if the table does not map it). A type listed more than once across the whole 'choices:' list -- in either shape -- is an IR error: this schema's own per-item validation cannot see a duplicate that uses a different shape the second time.

icon.description: A built-in catalogue name for this choice's icon, or the literal 'none' to explicitly draw no icon for it (distinct from simply not mentioning this choice's icon at all, which keeps the catalogue default). Mutually exclusive with 'glyph:'.

glyph.description: A codepoint in the vendored icon font that the catalogue does not name, written in Unicode notation: "U+F0BC". Mutually exclusive with 'icon:'. Checked against the font's own character map at build time, exactly like a plain 'icon' element's own 'glyph:'.

expression.description: An expression over data sources, palette entries and literals. A bare number is accepted for the common case of a literal bound (max: 10000) and needs no quoting.

colorExpression.description: A palette reference, a literal colour, or an expression yielding one.

font.description: One 'fonts:' entry -- either a custom bitmap font baked from a TrueType/OpenType source at build time (only the glyphs the design actually uses are rendered into the sheet), or a device-resident scalable face reached through Graphics.getVectorFont at draw time (plan 11) -- the only way to get rotated or curved text ('curve:' on a 'text' element), since Dc.drawAngledText/drawRadialText refuse a resource font outright. 'source:' and 'face:' are mutually exclusive and jointly required, so an entry naming neither, or both, is rejected here rather than read as an unknown-key mismatch.

bakedFont.description: A custom bitmap font, baked from a TrueType/OpenType source at build time.

source.description: Path to a TrueType/OpenType file, relative to the design file.

size.description: The em size to rasterise this font at, per device. px or %r only -- a sheet is baked before any element is placed, so there is no parent box for % and no font in scope for pt; the compiler reports the other two against your own line. '%r' scales with each device's own screen; 'px' is the same pixel count everywhere.

glyphs.description: The characters to bake. Omit to let the compiler derive the set from every string the design can render.

antialias.description: Bitmap fonts default to 1-bit to save runtime RAM. Anti-aliasing costs memory (SDK: Resources, Fonts).

monospace.description: Bake every glyph at one shared advance, the widest the set needs. A digital clock in a proportional face shifts as its digits change ('1' is narrower than '0'); one cell width stops that. Works on a proportional source as well as a monospaced one -- the cell is measured from the glyphs actually baked.

align.description: Where a glyph's ink sits inside its cell. Only meaningful with monospace: true, and an error without it.

if_unavailable.description: Vector-font key. A build error here: a baked font is rasterised from your own 'source:' at build time, so it is never unavailable on any device -- there is nothing for 'if_unavailable:' to govern. Parsed here (rather than rejected as an unknown key) purely so the compiler can name that reason instead of jsonschema's generic message.

vectorFont.description: A device-resident scalable face, drawn through Graphics.getVectorFont instead of a baked sheet. Only Garmin's own fixed catalogue of on-device faces is reachable this way -- about 14 Latin ones, published on 44 of the 136 watch-face-capable devices in the reference (docs/research/12-vector-fonts.md §3.2) -- and nothing can add a face to that list, so an author's own typeface can never be one. 'glyphs:', 'monospace:', 'align:' and 'antialias:' are all properties of baking a sheet, and this schema still parses them here (rather than rejecting them as unknown keys) purely so the compiler can name the actual mistake -- 'a vector font has no sheet' -- instead of jsonschema's generic 'unknown key' message; every one of the four is a build error on a 'face:' entry.

glyphs.description: Baked-font key. A build error here: a vector font is never rasterised to a sheet, so there is no glyph set to restrict.

antialias.description: Baked-font key. A build error here: there is no bitmap sheet for anti-aliasing to apply to.

monospace.description: Baked-font key. A build error here: there is no baked cell for a glyph's advance to be fixed to.

align.description: Baked-font key. A build error here: with no baked cell (see 'monospace:'), there is nowhere for a glyph's ink to sit inside it.

face.description: The device-resident face name(s) to ask Graphics.getVectorFont for, tried in the order given -- a string for one, or an array for several acceptable alternatives. Resolved per target device at build time to the single face that device actually publishes; ':face' is then emitted as that one resolved string, never the array. Garmin's own runtime array fallback is deliberately not used here: it would pick a face at draw time, so the build could not say which one renders, or measure the layout box against it. A device that publishes none of the listed faces fails this font's availability gates -- governed by 'if_unavailable:'.

size.description: The pixel height to draw this face at, per device. px or %r only, the same rule a baked font's 'size:' follows -- but unlike a baked font, nothing is rasterised at this size at build time: Graphics.getVectorFont takes it directly, in pixels, at draw time, so one face serves any number of sizes with no extra sheets.

if_unavailable.description: What to do on a target device that fails to publish any of the listed 'face:' names, or lacks Graphics.getVectorFont entirely. 'error' (the default) fails the build, naming the device, the face(s) asked for, and the faces that device does publish -- a missing clock is not a cosmetic problem. 'hide' lets every element using this font simply not draw on that one device; every other device is unaffected. This is a build-time guarantee only: Graphics.getVectorFont can still return null at runtime even when every build-time gate passed (the platform offers no other way to fail), and the generated code always null-checks regardless of this setting -- there is no way to promise a live face never goes missing, only that it was published at build time. An element using this font may override this outright with its own 'if_unavailable:'.

curve.description: Bends a 'text' element's content along a straight line or around a circle, through Dc.drawAngledText/Dc.drawRadialText. Both calls refuse a resource font outright ('These APIs only support scalable fonts and do not support custom fonts loaded as resources', SDK Core Topics: Graphics, Scalable Fonts) -- so the element's 'font:' must name a 'face:' (vector) 'fonts:' entry; a baked or system font under 'curve:' is a build error quoting that same sentence.

style.description: 'angled' draws the text along one straight line through 'at:', tilted by 'angle:'. 'radial' sweeps it around a circle -- 'at:' is then the CENTRE OF THE CIRCLE, not a point the text passes through, and 'radius:' is the circle's own radius. 'radius:'/'direction:' are rejected on 'angled': there is no circle for either to describe.

angle.description: Not one convention -- 'angled' and 'radial' use 'angle:' for genuinely different kinds of quantity, despite sharing units ('deg'/'rad'/'turn'). For 'style: radial', a POSITION: where around the circle the text starts, in this format's universal 12 o'clock = 0, clockwise-positive direction convention -- the same one every other angle in the format uses (arc/hand/pattern start angles); the compiler converts to Garmin's 3-o'clock/counter-clockwise one. For 'style: angled', a ROTATION: how far the text's own baseline is tilted away from level, clockwise positive, where '0deg' means unrotated (level text) rather than 'pointing at 12 o'clock' -- deliberately a different zero from every direction angle in the format, because conflating the two made the common cases (a level bezel numeral, a gently tilted ribbon) need '90deg' while '0deg', which reads like 'no rotation', stood the text on end.

radius.description: 'radial' only: the circle's own radius, the same unit rules 'at:'/'radius:' already use elsewhere. Required with 'style: radial'. Schema-legal but rejected as a build error under 'style: angled' -- parsed here rather than turned away as an unknown key, so the compiler can name the actual mistake (an angled line has no circle for it to describe) instead of jsonschema's generic message, the same 'text-antialias' precedent 'wfb.ir.builder' already follows.

direction.description: 'radial' only: which way the text runs around the circle starting at 'angle:'. Schema-legal but rejected as a build error under 'style: angled', for the same reason 'radius:' is.

faceAod.description: Face-wide always-on-display defaults (docs/plans/14-aod.md §2.2), for elements/groups whose own ancestry says nothing.

default.description: Whether an element with no 'aod:' anywhere in its own ancestry draws in AOD. 'hide' (the default) is safe: an unconverted design lights nothing extra. Fills only where nothing in the ancestry spoke -- unlike an explicit 'aod: hide' on a group, this is not sticky, so one element's own 'aod: show' still applies even under a face default of 'hide'.

dim.description: Scale the luminance of every colour the AOD frame draws (docs/plans/14-aod.md §4.5): each 8-bit channel times 'dim', rounded to the nearest integer. 1 (or omitting 'dim:') is identity -- no dimming code is emitted at all. 0 is rejected outright (exclusiveMinimum): it would make every undimmed-by-override colour black, indistinguishable from 'aod: hide'. An explicit 'color:'/'track_color:'/'icon_color:' inside an element's own 'aod:' override block is never dimmed -- it is the author's final word.

mask.description: A moving 2x2 pixel mask over the whole AOD frame (docs/plans/16-aod-pixel-mask.md): one pixel in each on-screen 2x2 tile stays lit, the other three are forced black, and which pixel of the tile is lit moves to a 4-neighbour once a minute (phase = minute mod 4). On (the default) unless set to false. No pixel is lit for two consecutive minutes and every pixel is lit at most one minute in four, cutting lit-pixel count and luminance to about a quarter of the unmasked frame. Stacks with 'dim:'.

lint.description: Suppress a face-level AOD lint (currently only 'aod-empty') -- there is no single element to hang an ordinary 'lint: {allow: [...]}' on for a face-wide check.

aodText.description: 'aod:' on a 'text' element (docs/plans/14-aod.md §2.3): 'hide' | 'show' | an override block reusing 'text's own 'color:'/'font:'/'format:'/'outline:', plus 'visible:'. An empty block ('aod: {}') means 'show'. 'outline:' replaces the awake ring whole, in the element's own 'outline:' grammar: 'none' drops the ring in AOD; a colour or '{color, width}' draws that ring instead, whether or not the element has one while awake.

aodShape.description: 'aod:' on a 'shape' element: 'hide' | 'show' | an override block reusing 'shape's own 'color:'/'thickness:'/'filled:', plus 'visible:'.

aodProgress.description: 'aod:' on a 'progress' element: 'hide' | 'show' | an override block reusing 'progress's own 'color:'/'track_color:'/'thickness:', plus 'visible:'.

aodIcon.description: 'aod:' on an 'icon' element: 'hide' | 'show' | an override block reusing 'icon's own 'color:', plus 'visible:'.

aodGraph.description: 'aod:' on a 'graph' element: 'hide' | 'show' | an override block reusing 'graph's own 'color:'/'thickness:'/'bar_width:', plus 'visible:'.

aodComplicationSlot.description: 'aod:' on a 'complication_slot' element: 'hide' | 'show' | an override block reusing its own 'color:'/'icon_color:'/'font:', plus 'visible:'.

aodHands.description: 'aod:' on a 'hands' element: 'hide' | 'show' | an override block reusing 'color:'/'thickness:', applied uniformly to every part of every hand in the set (docs/plans/14-aod.md §5.1), plus 'visible:'.

aodPattern.description: 'aod:' on a 'pattern' element: 'hide' | 'show' | an override block reusing 'color:'/'thickness:'/'font:', applied uniformly to every part (docs/plans/14-aod.md §5.1), plus 'visible:'.

aodGroup.description: 'aod:' on a 'group': 'hide' | 'show' | an override block allowing the union of every kind a descendant might allow (docs/plans/14-aod.md §2.3), plus 'visible:'. Pushed down to descendants key by key -- see the top-level 'aod:' resolution rule.

outline.description: The stamped-ring outline (research 13/14, plan 15): draws the text N times at small pixel offsets in this colour, then once more, unshifted, in the element's own 'color:' -- the fill pass every text element already has. 'none' (the default) draws no ring at all, byte-identical to today. The shorthand form (a bare colour expression) is 'width: 2' with that colour.

width.description: Ring width in pixels, not a Length -- always pixels, on every device, the same way a pattern's own 'count:' is a bare integer with no unit (docs/guide/patterns.md). Capped at 3 -- a build error above that, not a schema bound, so the message can cite research 14's own numbers (D6, plan 15 §13). Never %/%r: the ring is a fixed visual stroke weight, the same way Garmin's own engine strokes at a fixed 2.0px regardless of device (research 13 §2.1).

position.description: A position relative to an anchor on the parent box. Either cartesian (dx/dy) or polar (angle/radius) -- polar is first-class because 115 of 164 devices are round.

length.description: px (device pixels), % (of the parent box on the axis being resolved), %r (of the screen's minor radius), or pt (multiples of the element's font pixel height). A bare number means px.

angle.description: Degrees, 12 o'clock = 0, clockwise positive. Converted to Garmin's drawArc convention by the compiler.

modes.description: Which power modes draw this element: 'active' (awake) and/or 'low_power' (MIP partial update). Mode is structural, not styling: AMOLED forbids onPartialUpdate entirely while MIP depends on it. The always-on-display sleep frame on an AMOLED target is governed by 'aod:' instead (docs/plans/14-aod.md) -- 'always_on' was removed outright (D3): it is a schema error naming 'aod:' as its replacement (wfb/validate.py).

visible.description: Draw this element only while this expression is true. It must type as a boolean -- use a comparison ('activity.steps > 0'), 'and'/'or'/'not', or a '?:' whose branches are booleans; there is no truthiness rule, so a bare Number is an error. Absent means hidden: if the condition reads a source the device cannot supply, the element is not drawn. There is deliberately no 'when_absent:' for visibility -- 'when_absent:' picks a substitute *value*, and there is no substitute for existence. On a 'group' this gates the whole subtree: the condition is conjoined into every element beneath it. A hidden element still occupies its box for the geometry, overlap and safe-area checks, and still owns its 'on_hold:' region -- see docs/limitations.md.

reason.description: Required. A suppression without a stated reason is how linters get disabled wholesale.

points.description: A polygon's vertices, each resolved against the parent box exactly as a line's `to:` is. Dc.fillPolygon documents a 64-point limit (Toybox/Graphics/Dc.html).

filled.description: false draws the outline at `thickness` instead of filling. Not accepted on `arc` (the platform has no filled-arc primitive) and `filled: false` is not accepted on `polygon` (Dc has no drawPolygon).

align.description: rectangle, rounded_rectangle, ellipse, circle, arc only -- not polygon or line (docs/guide/placement.md, "Placement: at: and align:").

vertical_align.description: rectangle, rounded_rectangle, ellipse, circle, arc only -- not polygon or line (docs/guide/placement.md, "Placement: at: and align:").

value.description: A data source path, or an expression over sources. Mutually exclusive with text.

format.description: A Python-style format spec: {:d}, {:.1f}, or strftime-style codes such as {:%H:%M} for a time source. With 'units:', a {unit} field shows the displayed unit's label (km or mi, °C or °F, m or ft, km/h or mph).

units.description: Convert 'value:' to the wearer's units (ADR 0005 §4): 'auto' follows the watch's own distance/elevation/temperature setting (System.DeviceSettings) at runtime, 'metric'/'statute' fix one system. 'value:' must be exactly one source with a physical quantity (activity.distance, ambient.altitude, weather.temperature, weather.wind_speed, ...); the converted value is a Float in km/mi, m/ft, °C/°F or km/h/mph. Omit to show the source's own unit, unconverted.

font.description: A custom font (font.<name>) or a system font (FONT_MEDIUM, FONT_NUMBER_HOT, ...).

when_absent.description: Required for a nullable source. Absence is the normal case on this platform, so the format refuses to guess.

curve.description: Bends this text along a line or around an arc, instead of drawing it upright with plain Dc.drawText. Requires 'font:' to name a 'face:' (vector) 'fonts:' entry -- a baked or system font here is a build error, since Dc.drawAngledText/drawRadialText refuse a resource font outright.

outline.description: Draws this text's string N times at small pixel offsets in a ring colour, then once more, unshifted, in 'color:' -- the stamped ring (research 13/14, plan 15). 'none' (the default) draws no ring at all, byte-identical to today.

if_unavailable.description: Overrides this element's font's own 'if_unavailable:' outright -- only meaningful when 'font:' names a 'face:' (vector) font; a build error on a baked or system font, since nothing there can ever be unavailable. 'error' fails the build naming the device and the face(s) it lacks; 'hide' makes this one element not draw on a device that fails the font's availability gates, leaving every other element that shares the font unaffected. Omit to inherit the font's own 'if_unavailable:' (itself 'error' by default).

style.description: arc is setPenWidth + drawArc. Garmin has no filled-sector primitive anywhere in the API, so thickness is a pen width and inner/outer radii are deliberately not offered.

when_absent.description: Required for a nullable value or max. A progress element has no placeholder: there is no substitute *text* for a fill fraction, so the choice is hide or a fallback expression.

icon.description: A name from the built-in icon catalogue, or any single glyph from the vendored icon font. Mutually exclusive with icon_for. A bitmap-font glyph, drawn with drawText -- not a hand-drawn primitive.

glyph.description: A codepoint in the vendored icon font that the catalogue does not name, written in Unicode notation: "U+F0BC". The explicit form of the bare character `icon:` also accepts -- greppable and visible in a diff, where the character itself is not. Checked against the font's own character map at build time. Mutually exclusive with icon and icon_for.

icon_for.description: Choose the glyph at runtime from a bound value, instead of a fixed icon: name. Currently accepts only a weather.condition* source (see wfb sources) -- the glyph is resolved on-device through a generated lookup covering all of Weather.CONDITION_*, mirroring wfb.icons.weather_icon_for_condition(). Mutually exclusive with icon.

series.description: A name from the series catalogue (`wfb series`): heart_rate; steps, calories, distance, floors_climbed, active_minutes; forecast_temperature, forecast_precipitation_chance, forecast_cloud_cover, forecast_uv_index, forecast_wind_speed, forecast_humidity; daily_high_temperature, daily_low_temperature, daily_precipitation_chance. None of these needs a permission; SensorHistory-backed series (pressure, stress, elevation, Body Battery) and solar are not available to a watch face at all -- see docs/limitations.md.

range.description: A duration ('30m', '4h', '7d') or a bare integer sample count. heart_rate passes a duration straight through to getHeartRateHistory and bins it at runtime; every other series converts a duration to a count at build time using its own natural interval (1 day for the activity and daily-forecast series, 1 hour for the hourly-forecast ones) -- asking for more than a documented maximum (getHistory()'s 7 days) is a build error, not a silent clamp.

buckets.description: Time bins for a time-binned series read over a duration -- i.e. heart_rate with a duration range. Default 40. An error naming the series on anything else.

style.description: line (setPenWidth + drawLine per segment), area (one fillPolygon, capped at 62 samples -- Dc.fillPolygon's own 64-point limit minus the two corners that close the outline) or bars (fillRectangle per bucket).

thickness.description: style: line only -- the pen width.

bar_width.description: style: bars only -- centred in each slot.

min.description: auto (the default) uses the series' own extent -- the iterator's getMin() for heart_rate, the collected values' extent for every other series. A number or an expression compiles like any other bound value.

max.description: See min. Two fixed bounds with min >= max is a build error.

complicationSlotElement.description: The native Data axis: a slot the wearer re-points at a different Garmin metric, on the watch, with the editor's own instant preview. Draws an icon chosen at runtime from the wearer's pick (every native complication type has one -- run 'wfb complications'/see wfb.icons.COMPLICATION_ICON) plus the reading itself, rendered as the watch reports it (toString(), except a Float or Double, rounded to three significant figures with trailing zeros removed), since the concrete value type genuinely varies by choice -- see 'format:' below.

slot.description: Which declared 'config: data:' slot this element shows, as 'config.data.<name>'.

font.description: A custom font (font.<name>) or a system font (FONT_MEDIUM, FONT_NUMBER_HOT, ...), for the reading. Defaults to FONT_SMALL.

icon_size.description: Visual height of the icon chosen from the wearer's pick. Omit to draw no icon. px or %r only. Superseded 2026-09-13: this used to also be rejected when the slot's own 'choices:' is 'any', since the set of icons such a slot could need was unbounded -- lifted once every native complication type had a catalogue icon (wfb.icons.COMPLICATION_ICON covers all 42 now); 'any' now resolves against that whole table, and a type it does not map (a Connect IQ-app complication) simply draws no icon.

color.description: Must not be nullable -- there is no 'when_absent:' for this element's own appearance, only for the pulled reading.

icon_position.description: Where the icon sits relative to the reading. Needs 'icon_size:' -- an error naming why, without it. Default left.

icon_gap.description: The space between icon and reading. px or %r only, and must not be negative. Needs 'icon_size:' -- an error naming why, without it. Default 4px (today's fixed gap).

icon_color.description: The icon's own colour, distinct from the reading's 'color:'. Must not be nullable, for the same reason 'color:' must not be. Needs 'icon_size:' -- an error naming why, without it. Defaults to 'color:' (today's only behaviour: one colour for the icon and the reading alike).

label.description: none (default): just the value. short/long: Complication.shortLabel/.longLabel, drawn before the value when the device supplies one.

unit.description: Append Complication.unit's suffix after the value (e.g. 'm', 'm/s', '°C') when the device supplies one. Default false.

when_absent.description: Governs the pulled reading only -- the icon, chosen from the slot's configured type rather than its current value, still draws either way. hide (default): the reading blanks, leaving the icon. placeholder: needs 'placeholder:'.

format.description: Not accepted -- an error naming why: the pulled value's concrete type varies by which choice the wearer makes, so one format string cannot be right for all of them. Accepted here only so 'wfb validate' can report that against your own line instead of a generic "additional property" error.

handsElement.description: Analog hands (plan 04): places a declared 'hands:' set on screen. 'at:' is the axis -- every part of the set is measured from it, and the element's extent is the disc it sweeps, not a box. No 'size:' (there is no box, only the axis), no 'on_hold:' (a moving hand has no fixed hit region -- hold a group around it instead), and 'static: true' is rejected (a buffer is painted once and never refilled, and a hand's angle is the time) -- accepted here, like every other element, only so the compiler can say so against your own line instead of a generic 'unknown key'.

at.description: The axis every hand in this set rotates about, on screen. May be off-centre.

seconds.description: Whether the set's second hand draws. 'awake' (default): drawn while awake, hidden while asleep -- a once-a-minute sleeping update would otherwise freeze it at whatever second that update landed on. 'never': the second hand is not drawn at all. An element whose set has no 'second:' hand may not set this. 'always' is reserved (not implemented -- see docs/limitations.md) and is refused with a friendly error, not this enum.

handSet.description: One named hand set (plan 04 §5.1): a shape, like a fonts: entry, not something drawn on its own -- it is placed by a 'type: hands' element naming it. Any of hour:/minute:/second: may be present, and at least one must be -- a set with only 'second:' is a small-seconds subdial.

hand.description: One hand: a default colour for its parts, plus the parts themselves, drawn in this order, pointing at 12 o'clock, in a frame whose origin is the axis.

color.description: Default colour for every part of this hand that declares none of its own. A hand colour may not read data -- palette, literal and config.* only (and conditionals over those).

handPart.description: One primitive of a hand, in the hand's own frame: origin = the axis, +x right, +y down (so the tip is at negative dy). 'anchor:' is rejected -- the axis is the anchor. Only the keys the chosen 'shape:' reads are accepted: polygon reads 'points'; rectangle reads 'at' (default the axis), 'size', 'align' and 'vertical_align'; line reads 'at' (default the axis), 'to' and 'thickness' (default 1px); circle reads 'at' (default the axis), 'radius', 'filled' (default true), 'thickness' (only when 'filled: false'), 'align' and 'vertical_align'. 'filled: false' is rejected on polygon and rectangle -- there is no drawPolygon. 'align'/'vertical_align' (plan 07 phase D) place the box in the part's own frame, before it turns with the hand -- see docs/guide/placement.md, "Placement: at: and align:"; not accepted on polygon (every vertex is its own position) or line ('at:'/'to:' are its two ends).

shape.description: The four rotatable primitives are polygon/rectangle/line/circle. rounded_rectangle, ellipse, arc, text and icon are recognised here only so the compiler can reject each with its own platform reason (docs/guide/analog-hands.md) instead of a bare 'not one of ...'.

points.description: A polygon part's vertices, 3 to 64, each a handPosition measured from the axis.

color.description: Overrides the hand's own default colour for this part only. Same data-binding restriction as the hand's own 'color:'.

min_1px.description: As authored, or omitted to inherit the owning 'type: hands' element's own resolved value. This part's own value wins outright over its element's -- one 'hands:' set can be placed by more than one 'type: hands' element, so a shared part's effective value can differ per placement.

handPosition.description: A position within a hand's own frame, measured from the axis -- there is no anchor, because the axis already is one. Cartesian (dx/dy) or polar (angle/radius, clockwise from 12 o'clock), px or %r only.

handLength.description: px or %r only -- a hand's own frame has no parent box for % and no font in scope for pt. %r is the screen's minor radius, so a hand scales between screens the same way the dial does. A bare number means px.

patternCurve.description: curve: on a pattern's own 'shape: text' part (plan 11 slice 2) -- the same bend a 'text' element's own 'curve:' gives it, through the same Dc.drawAngledText/Dc.drawRadialText, with one difference: 'angle:' is in the TEMPLATE'S OWN LOCAL FRAME, for copy 0. A radial pattern turns every later copy's angle right along with its anchor -- the same way a pattern 'shape: arc' part's own 'start_angle:' already turns with the copy -- so an author writes one angle per part (e.g. 0deg, tangent to the copy's own radius), not one per copy; a linear pattern never turns, so every copy simply keeps this angle unchanged. Otherwise identical to the 'curve' definition: 'style:' is the required discriminator ('angled'/'radial'), 'radius:'/'direction:' are rejected on 'angled'. The one real difference from '#/$defs/curve' is 'radius:', which is a handLength here (px or %r only) rather than a length -- a pattern part has no parent box for '%' and no font in scope for 'pt' in this position, the same restriction every other pattern-part length already carries.

style.description: 'angled' draws this copy's own text along one straight line through its own anchor, tilted by 'angle:'. 'radial' sweeps it around a circle centred on that same anchor -- 'radius:' is the circle's own radius. 'radius:'/'direction:' are rejected on 'angled': there is no circle for either to describe.

angle.description: In this part's own local (copy-0) frame -- a radial pattern composes it with the copy's own rotation, the same way an 'arc' part's 'start_angle:' composes with 'start:'/'step:'. Not one convention, the same split '#/$defs/curve's own 'angle:' makes: for 'style: radial', a POSITION (12 o'clock = 0, clockwise positive -- where around the circle the text starts). For 'style: angled', a ROTATION ('0deg' = level/unrotated, clockwise positive -- how far the text's own baseline is tilted). A radial PATTERN with an 'angled' text part composing '0deg' with each copy's own rotation is what makes one 'angle: 0deg' sit tangent to every copy's own radius and read level at the top of the dial, without the author writing one angle per copy.

radius.description: 'radial' only: the circle's own radius, px or %r only (a pattern part's frame has no parent box for '%' and no font in scope for 'pt'). Required with 'style: radial'. Schema-legal but rejected as a build error under 'style: angled', the same 'text-antialias' precedent 'wfb.ir.builder' already follows elsewhere.

direction.description: 'radial' only: which way the text runs around the circle starting at 'angle:'. Schema-legal but rejected as a build error under 'style: angled', for the same reason 'radius:' is.

patternElement.description: One template of 1-16 primitives (plan 05: 'pattern'), drawn repeatedly -- turned about 'at:' ('pattern: radial') or stepped along {dx, dy} ('pattern: linear'). No 'size:' (the extent is computed from the drawn ink, not authored), no 'on_hold:' (a repeated template has no single fixed hit region -- hold a 'group' around it instead) -- accepted here, like every other element, only so the compiler can say so against your own line instead of a generic 'unknown key'. 'static: true' is accepted unless a colour reads a data source, which a buffer filled once would freeze (the ordinary static-binding error); a colour that reads only 'copy' is fixed per copy and fine there -- unlike 'hands', whose angle is the clock. A colour (the element's own or any part's) or a part 'visible:' may read a source that can be absent, but only with 'when_absent: hide' declared -- see 'when_absent' below.

pattern.description: 'radial': copies turn about 'at:', 'step' degrees apart. 'linear': copies step along {dx, dy} from 'at:'.

at.description: Radial: the centre every copy turns about. Linear: copy 0's own origin. An ordinary position, resolved against the parent box exactly like any other element's 'at:'.

count.description: How many copies. Dc draws one primitive per call -- there is no repeat/instancing call on this platform (docs/plans/05-patterns.md 1) -- so this is also how many times the device loops and rotates or translates the template.

step.description: Radial: the angle between consecutive copies, default 360deg / count; negative turns counter-clockwise; 0deg is an error. Linear: required, {dx, dy} -- either may be omitted (0). Writing an angle on a linear pattern, a {dx, dy} on a radial one, or omitting it on a linear one, are each build-time errors, not schema errors -- both shapes are accepted here so the compiler can name the real mistake against your own line.

start.description: Radial only: the angle of copy 0, default 0deg (12 o'clock). An error on a linear pattern -- {dx, dy} already places copy 0 via 'at:'.

skip.description: Copy indices (0-based, each less than 'count:', no duplicates) that are left undrawn -- room for another pattern's copies, e.g. the hour ticks' places in a 60-copy minute ring.

skip_every.description: Copies whose index is a multiple of this are left undrawn (0, N, 2N, ...) -- 2 to 'count:'.

color.description: Default colour for every part that declares none of its own. May read 'copy' -- the index of the copy being drawn, 0-based, bound nowhere else -- and any data source, including one that can be absent -- but a nullable source anywhere in the pattern (this colour, a part's colour, or a part's 'visible:') requires 'when_absent: hide' on the pattern (see 'when_absent'). e.g. "copy == (date.weekday + 5) % 7 ? palette.on : palette.off".

when_absent.description: Required once any colour (the element's own or any part's) or any part 'visible:' reads a source that can be absent. The only value is 'hide': absence hides the whole pattern -- every copy, every part -- because the reading is taken once per frame, before the loop, not once per copy. There is no 'placeholder:'/'fallback:' here: a pattern has no single value to substitute one for.

patternPart.description: One primitive of a pattern's template, in the same frame a hand part uses (plan 05 §5.2): origin = the pattern's own 'at:', +x right, +y down, drawn as copy 0 looks (radial: 12 o'clock; linear: no rotation). 'anchor:' is rejected -- the origin is the only reference point. Only the keys the chosen 'shape:' reads are accepted: polygon reads 'points'; rectangle reads 'at' (default the origin), 'size', 'align' and 'vertical_align'; line reads 'at' (default the origin), 'to' and 'thickness' (default 1px); circle reads 'at' (default the origin), 'radius', 'filled' (default true), 'thickness' (only when 'filled: false'), 'align' and 'vertical_align'; arc reads 'radius', 'thickness' (default 1px), 'start_angle' and 'sweep' (default 360deg) -- never 'at:' or alignment, because an arc is always centred on the copy's own origin (docs/plans/05-patterns.md D3); text reads 'at' (default the origin), 'value' xor 'text', 'format', 'font', 'align', 'vertical_align', 'curve', 'if_unavailable' and 'outline' (plan 06 §3, plan 11 slice 2, plan 15 slice 2) -- upright glyphs whose anchor turns (radial) or steps (linear) with the copy, unlike a rectangle/circle part's box, which turns with the part (plan 07 phase D); with 'curve:' and a 'face:' (vector) 'font:', the glyphs themselves turn too, tangent to (or around) the copy's own position, not just the anchor; 'outline:' stamps a ring around this copy's own already-turned/stepped glyphs, exactly as on a standalone 'text' element. 'filled: false' is rejected on polygon and rectangle -- there is no drawPolygon. 'align'/'vertical_align' are not accepted on polygon (every vertex is its own position) or line ('at:'/'to:' are its two ends) -- see docs/guide/placement.md, "Placement: at: and align:".

shape.description: polygon/rectangle/line/circle/arc/text are the six primitives a pattern can repeat -- text is upright glyphs at an anchor point that turns (radial) or steps (linear) with the copy (plan 06 §3), unlike a hand part, which still rejects it (a bitmap font cannot rotate); with 'curve:' and a 'face:' font, a pattern's own text part can turn its glyphs too (plan 11 slice 2). rounded_rectangle, ellipse and icon are recognised here only so the compiler can reject each with its own platform reason (docs/guide/patterns.md) instead of a bare 'not one of ...'.

points.description: A polygon part's vertices, 3 to 64, each a handPosition measured from the origin.

color.description: Overrides the pattern's own default colour for this part only. Same rules as the pattern's own 'color:', 'copy' included.

visible.description: Draw this part only while this expression is true, evaluated separately for each copy -- 'copy' is bound here, the same as in a colour. Must type as a boolean, the same rule the element-level 'visible:' uses. Other parts, and other copies of this same part, are unaffected. Unlike the element-level 'visible:', a source here that can be absent is not 'absent means this part is hidden': the reading is taken once per frame, before the loop, so its absence hides the whole pattern under 'when_absent: hide' (see the pattern's own 'when_absent'), not just this part for this copy.

start_angle.description: 'shape: arc' only. The arc's own start angle as authored for copy 0; a radial pattern turns it with each copy (12 o'clock = 0, clockwise). Default 0deg.

sweep.description: 'shape: arc' only. How far the arc spans, clockwise positive, default 360deg (a full ring) when omitted.

value.description: 'shape: text' only. An expression for the glyphs this copy draws -- may read only 'copy' (the index of the copy being drawn, bound nowhere else in this key), so every copy's string is known at build time for font subsetting and extents. Mutually exclusive with 'text'.

text.description: 'shape: text' only. A fixed string, drawn the same for every copy. Mutually exclusive with 'value'.

format.description: 'shape: text' only, and only with 'value:'. A Python-style format spec: {:d}, {:02d}, {:.1f}.

font.description: 'shape: text' only. A custom font (font.<name>) or a system font (FONT_MEDIUM, FONT_NUMBER_HOT, ...). Default FONT_MEDIUM.

curve.description: 'shape: text' only, and only with a 'face:' (vector) 'font:' (plan 11 slice 2). Bends this copy's own text along a line or around a circle, exactly as a 'text' element's own 'curve:' does -- 'angle:' is in the part's own local (copy-0) frame; a radial pattern composes it with each copy's own rotation, so one angle serves every copy. A baked or system font here is a build error, the same 'text-curve' reasoning a 'text' element's own 'curve:' gives.

if_unavailable.description: 'shape: text' only, and only with a 'face:' (vector) 'font:'. Overrides that font's own 'if_unavailable:' outright for this part -- 'error' (the default) fails the build naming the device and the face(s) it lacks; 'hide' makes this one part not draw on a device that fails the font's availability gates, leaving every other part of the same pattern (and every other element sharing the font) unaffected. A build error on a baked or system font, since nothing there can ever be unavailable.

outline.description: 'shape: text' only (plan 15 slice 2). The stamped-ring outline, identical to a standalone 'text' element's own 'outline:' -- draws this copy's string N times at small screen-space pixel offsets in a ring colour, then once more, unshifted, in the part's own 'color:'. The offsets are applied to this copy's own already-rotated/translated anchor, after the pattern's own per-copy rotation and after the part's own 'curve:' angle -- never re-rotated themselves -- so the ring is not smeared by either transform. 'none' (the default) draws no ring at all, byte-identical to today.

align.description: 'shape: rectangle', 'circle' or 'text' only. On rectangle/circle, the box is placed in the part's own frame, before it turns or steps with the copy (plan 07 phase D); on text, only the anchor point moves this way -- the glyphs stay upright (plan 06 §3), unless 'curve:' turns the glyphs themselves too (plan 11 slice 2).

vertical_align.description: 'shape: rectangle', 'circle' or 'text' only. Same frame-vs-anchor distinction as 'align' above. Under 'curve: {style: radial}' all three values are accepted -- 'top'/'bottom' choose which side of the circle the line box falls on (Dc.drawRadialText's own baseline-on-the-circle behaviour without TEXT_JUSTIFY_VCENTER). 'bottom' is rejected under 'curve: {style: angled}', the same reason a 'text' element's own 'curve:' rejects it there.

min_1px.description: As authored, or omitted to inherit the owning pattern's own resolved value. This part's own value wins outright over its pattern's, applied on top of whichever copy repeats it.

patternStep.description: The offset between consecutive copies of a linear pattern: {dx, dy}, either may be omitted (0). Resolved against the parent box on the axis each measures ('dx' against width, 'dy' against height), then rounded to whole pixels once, so every gap between copies is identical (docs/plans/05-patterns.md D4).

patternLength.description: px, % (of the parent box on the axis being resolved) or %r (of the screen's minor radius) -- not pt: a linear pattern's step has no font in scope to measure against. A bare number means px.

onHold.description: Touch and hold this element to launch the glance or app that owns this complication type -- Complications.exitTo, the only exit a watch face has. Run `wfb complications` for the names. Hold is the only gesture a live watch face receives on any device: WatchFaceDelegate.onTap fires solely inside the on-device config editor. Also accepts 'auto': resolved at build time from this element's own value binding (a text's value: or icon_for:, a progress's value: -- never color:/track_color:/max:) via Source.launch_complication, erroring if that binding resolves no conventional target or more than one. On a complication_slot, only 'auto' is accepted (a fixed name is an error naming why) -- it opens whichever glance the wearer's own *current* pick belongs to, resolved on-device on every hold rather than to a fixed name at build time.

staticFlag.description: Draw this element once into an offscreen Graphics.BufferedBitmap and blit the buffer every frame instead of redrawing it. On a 'group' this covers the whole subtree; on a leaf it is one element on its own. The buffer comes from the separate graphics pool (1 MB on every supported target), not the 128 KB app budget, and a device without createBufferedBitmap -- or a failed allocation -- falls back to drawing the same content directly, so the face always renders. Constraints, all build-time errors: nothing in a static subtree may be bound to a data source (including 'visible:'), a graph or complication_slot may not be static, 'modes:' may not include 'low_power', 'static:' may not nest, and every element in a static subtree must declare the same 'modes:'. Static content is always drawn first, wherever it is written: the buffer is opaque and full-screen, so nothing can be under it, and the compiler hoists it to the front of draw order rather than rejecting the design -- where that swaps two overlapping elements round it warns (suppressible 'static-overlap'). See docs/guide/elements.md and docs/research/probes/static-buffer/.

antialias.description: Override the face-wide 'antialias:' default for this element. On a 'group' this is also the default for its whole subtree -- not a conjunction the way 'visible:' is, so a descendant's own 'antialias:' still wins outright over its group's. On 'shape', 'progress', 'graph', 'hands' and 'pattern' this flags the element's own Dc primitive drawing (for 'hands', every hand of the set; for 'pattern', every copy); on 'icon' and 'complication_slot' it flags the baked icon font -- two mechanisms gated in two different ways by the SDK (a resource attribute for a font, a runtime Dc call for a primitive), so they share this one key but not an implementation. Not accepted on 'text': a text element draws through a font declared in 'fonts:', one bitmap resource shared by every element that references it, so anti-aliasing cannot vary per element -- put it on that font's own 'antialias:' instead.

min_1px.description: Override the face-wide 'min_1px:' default for this element. On a 'group' this is also the default for its whole subtree -- not a conjunction the way 'visible:' is, so a descendant's own 'min_1px:' still wins outright over its group's. Clamps a nonzero '%'/'%r' size (width/height), thickness, 'bar_width:' or this element's own radius up to at least 1 px instead of letting it round away to nothing, sign preserved -- never a position, 'corner_radius:', a 'px'/'pt' length or an author-written exact 0. Not accepted on 'text', 'icon' or 'complication_slot': a font size already floors at 1 px on its own path, with no switch to set. See the top-level 'min_1px:' for the full rule, and the suppressible 'sub-pixel-length' lint it enables while this is off.
